morphology_as_written: plate-like (PL); SEM revealed structures closer to the desired pattern under both premixing temperatures (25 and 100 C)
varied: CTAB concentration, mixing order, premix temperature
mechanism_as_written: CTAB forms micelles under vigorous stirring that concentrate Hmim and Co-Hmim intermediates and exclude OH-, preventing hydroxide by-products; pre-mixing CTAB with Hmim matters most.
notes: Stirring refers to the premixing stage (1800 rpm); the autoclave stage is not described as stirred. 65.36 mmol Hmim and 2.179 mmol Co(OAc)2 in 64 mL water total (metal_conc_mM computed), 1800 rpm premixing, 150 mL autoclave. The paper's Table 1 lists the TARGET shape taken from a ZIF-8 morphology map; the observed shape is the SEM description quoted here.

morphology_as_written: more well-defined facets when CTAB is dissolved in MeIM before synthesis. However, all four evaluated synthesis conditions afford particles of varying sizes and irregular morphologies
varied: CTAB concentration, mixing order, premix temperature
notes: Targeted nanocubes (by analogy with the ZIF-8 map) were NOT obtained cleanly. This is a useful negative: a CTAB level that gives ZIF-8 cubes does not transfer directly to ZIF-67 under these conditions.

morphology_as_written: vigorous stirring and emulsion formation yielded particles with higher crystallinity, more regular morphologies, and more homogeneous size distributions than those synthesized under weak stirring conditions
varied: stirring speed (450 vs 1800 rpm) and temperature (120 vs 140 C)
notes: Stirring effect rather than a named shape. Crystallinity higher at 140 C than at 120 C. Contrasts with cravillon2012, where unstirred solutions gave more homogeneous ZIF-8 crystals; the authors attribute the difference to micelle formation.
